It now looks for ISO date-times in the text and for JSON object keys that name a time (time, timestamp, date, created, updated, *_at); field names listed as values are not keys.
procedure: Helpers: Ctx, Edit, Result and the canonical-output functions are imported from probes.py (the first experiment's runner); Ctx is subclassed here for Streak (clone, manifest, consumer name). `str.replace` edits assert their count first; E5a's old string ends with a newline (the line-ending anchor of the prereg).

Commits in the scratch clones use `-c user.name=probe -c user.email=probe@example.invalid`; the GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* names of the base Ctx are removed from the environment so that these flags apply (the dates stay fixed).
Item notation: the code writes the auth item as 'as_user:ann'; comparisons normalise ':' after as_user to a space, nothing else.

D1 item: the prereg gives no item for endpoint_missing; the expected item is the empty string (the claim 'endpoint' has none). Likewise the CHANGED rows of endpoint_added, endpoint_removed and the status/auth kinds have `where` empty; field kinds have 'request' or 'response'.

The expected CHANGED set of D7 (17 endpoint_removed + 24 endpoint_added, all unrelied) is derived from the clean export's 24 `/v1/` endpoints minus the 7 imported ones, as the prereg's counts say; the 26 endpoints count is checked on a `contracts export` run on the drifted clone.
R1 statuses: the 26 expect_status lists below are copied from R1 (r1-streak-surface.json, templates), with names `{...}` written `{}` as the export does.

W3 evidence that nothing is started: PATH is prefixed with shims for docker, go, mysqld, mysql and streak-api that log any call and exit 127; a `ps` sampler (20 ms) records the process command lines seen during the check; the clone's `git status --ignored` and bin/ are compared before and after. The check's own Python child (lattice.contracts.live) is expected: it loads the spec and refuses before any provider process.
S1's git calls use --no-optional-locks so that `git status` cannot refresh the real repository's index; `find -newer` excludes .git only.
T1 wall times are whole subprocess times (interpreter start included); the check's own elapsed_s is recorded beside them.

W4 compares each of the 6 outputs (exit code, stdout, stderr) of the working tree and of the detached worktree lattice-contracts-base (HEAD c0cdefc, lattice/workspace.py unmodified, checked at run time), and records which lattice/workspace.py a child imports under each PYTHONPATH and whether lattice.contracts exists there.
